## claude.ai Todoist

## Todoist Task and Project Management Tools

You have access to comprehensive Todoist management tools for personal productivity and team collaboration. Use these tools to help users manage tasks, projects, sections, comments, and assignments effectively.

### Core Capabilities:
- Create, update, complete, and search tasks with rich metadata (priorities, due dates, durations, assignments)
- Manage projects and sections with flexible organization
- Handle comments and collaboration features
- Bulk assignment operations for team workflows
- Get overviews and insights about workload and progress

### Choosing between tools

What each tool does and how to fill its parameters is in the tool's own description and input schema. This section covers only what those cannot: which tool to reach for, and how tools relate to each other.

**Dates**

- To move a task to a different date use **reschedule-tasks**, never **update-tasks**. update-tasks replaces the whole due string, which destroys recurrence on recurring tasks.
- Never send a task's existing projectId, sectionId or parentId back to **update-tasks** — those fields are treated as a move.
- All dates respect the user's timezone.

**Finding things**

- For "what did I complete?", call **user-info** for the asker's user ID, then **find-activity** with objectType="task", eventType="completed", initiatorId, and dateFrom/dateTo. Without initiatorId the answer covers every collaborator. find-activity reports completion events, including each occurrence of a recurring task; **find-completed-tasks** lists completed tasks, which is not the same question.
- To resolve a person's name or email to a user ID, or to answer "who is X?", use **find-project-collaborators** with just a searchTerm. It covers every shared project you can access plus yourself, so an empty result means they collaborate on none of them — not that they do not exist.

## claude.ai freddy Oura MCP
freddy is the user's personal health-data server: sleep, workouts, recovery, HRV, glucose and body metrics from their connected sources (wearables, rings, CGMs, training platforms, gym logs, sensors).

How to query: call list_metrics once per conversation to discover the exact metric names this user has — names are provider-specific (e.g. wellness_sleepSecs, blood_glucose_avg), so never guess generic English names. Then call query_metrics with those names; the default window is the last 7 days.

list_metrics groups metrics under a `Source: <name>` header per connected source. On an account with many sources it can report that a source was not fully listed — follow the continuation hint it gives you (provider, and `after` when present) before concluding a metric does not exist. Pass `provider` to list one source at a time.

Account limits: This account can query the last 7 days of synced data. It queries one connected source at a time (currently showing Oura); other connected sources keep syncing in the background but are not queryable. Responses cap at 500 rows (fewer with include_raw); a truncated response states the date range it covered and how to continue.

Long time ranges: pass `start` and `end` (YYYY-MM-DD) — required for windows beyond 1 year. For multi-month or multi-year questions pass granularity: "week" or "month" to get avg/min/max buckets that fit years of data in one response; prefer daily-summary metrics (the *_avg / *_min / *_max variants shown by list_metrics) over per-reading metrics, and when a response reports truncation, follow its continuation hint to page backwards through the range.

Specific dates: the window is one contiguous range, so to compare non-adjacent dates (e.g. two workouts weeks apart) make one call per date with `start` and `end` set to that date. One wide range spanning both returns newest-first and can truncate the older date away — that is a truncated response, not an absence of data, so never report the older date as missing without querying it on its own.

I found it — in `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/todoist-client.ts` (`makeTodoistTask`), tasks/e-blasts are pushed to Todoist using the `due_date` field, not `due_datetime`:

```js
due_date: dueDate,   // e.g. "2026-09-15" — date only, no time
```

That value is just the task's/e-blast's `dueDate` field (`artifacts/api-server/src/routes/todoist.ts:33,77`), a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` string with no time component attached.

**So there's no default time being set at all** — the sync intentionally sends an all-day due date. In the Todoist app these show up as due "today"/that date with no clock time, not e.g. 9:00 AM or any other default hour. (If you compare that to a task you create by hand in Todoist with a time typed in, that one would show a time; these synced ones won't.)

content.text:
Confirmed — the current code only sends a bare `due_date` (date-only) to Todoist; there's no time logic and no timezone handling anywhere in this repo. The 11:59 PM you're seeing is Todoist's own behavior for date-only due dates (its calendar/list views render dateless-time tasks as ending at 23:59), not something our sync sets.

To fix it, I'd switch the sync to send an actual time of day. Two ways to do that:

questions.question: What default time should synced tasks/e-blasts get in Todoist?
Should the default time be hardcoded, or configurable later (e.g. via env var)?

options.label: Hardcode it (Recommended)
options.description: Simplest — a single constant in todoist-client.ts you can change anytime

options.label: Env var
options.description: Add a TODOIST_DEFAULT_TIME env var so it can be changed without a code deploy

content.text:
Confirmed those typecheck errors are pre-existing (present even with my change stashed out — looks like generated codegen is stale/out of sync, unrelated to this fix). My edit itself is clean and isolated to `todoist-client.ts`.

**What I changed** — `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/todoist-client.ts`: instead of sending a bare `due_date` (date-only, which Todoist renders as if due at end-of-day/11:59 PM), it now sends `due_string: "YYYY-MM-DD 09:00"` with `due_lang: "en"`, so Todoist's date parser resolves it to 9:00 AM in your Todoist account's own timezone. This applies to both task and e-blast syncs (both route through the same `makeTodoistTask` helper). To change the default later, just edit the `DEFAULT_TASK_TIME` constant at the top of that file.

This will apply going forward on the next sync — it updates existing synced tasks (since sync does a POST update for tasks that already have a `todoistTaskId`), so previously-synced items will pick up 9:00 AM on the next `/sync` run too, not just newly created ones.

Would you like me to commit this change?

content: We're fixing Todoist sync so tasks stop showing as due 11:59 PM — I set a 9:00 AM default and made the code change. Next: confirm and commit it. (disable recaps in /config)

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Default synced Todoist tasks to 9:00 AM instead of 11:59 PM

Switch from due_date (date-only) to due_string with a fixed 09:00
time so tasks/e-blasts synced to Todoist show a sensible time
instead of Todoist's end-of-day default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
